messages:
sre-bot: ALERT: p95/p99 spike detected for /v1/complete across hosted-us-west-1. Spike window start 07:22 UTC. Error rate up from 0.05% -> 1.9% on some customer routes.

eli: support queue shows multiple urgent tickets (TopRetail, MediQ) reporting repeated 502s and long tails ~12-25s. Escalating to infra.

vikas: quick look at infra graphs: a cluster of GPU nodes show NVMe queue depth jumps and host-side CPU steal; per-node p99 correlates with device avg wait spikes. Also seeing occasional 'nvme_core: controller reset' entries in syslog.

ke: past 24h we pushed driver 538.13 and a minor kernel backport (pci hotfix) to a set of pre-prod hosts; a small subset was promoted to serving late-night. Canary bench didn't exercise snapshot/loadgen.

toni: repro locally: run 60 concurrent clients hitting /v1/complete on a host with the new driver while running an fio mixed small random write workload against the NVMe. Repro yields p95 ~1.3s -> 2.6s, p99 spikes to 10-18s.

toni: repro commands:
```
# generate inference load
wrk -t8 -c60 -d180s http://host-test-12:8080/v1/complete?model=redwood-std
# run backend IO stress
fio --name=meta_stress --rw=randrw --rwmixread=70 --bs=4k --ioengine=libaio --iodepth=32 --size=2G --runtime=180
```

vikas: sample dmesg excerpt from affected host:
```
[23456.789012] nvme nvme0: controller reset due to timeout
[23456.789345] nvme nvme0: Completion queue timeout
[23456.790000] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:af:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
[23456.791200] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 234234
```

ke: iostat snapshot:
```
Device r/s w/s rkB/s wkB/s avgqu-sz await svctm %util
nvme0n1 320.5 720.1 12800 32000 45.2 28.7 0.95 99.3
nvme5n1 12.4 14.1 96 112 0.1 0.9 0.10 2.1
```

eli: immediate mitigation proposals: 1) evacuate affected nodes from serving pool, 2) pause heavy background ops (snapshots/backups) for 60m, 3) start driver revert for the affected batch, 4) throttle per-host concurrency to 40.

support-bot: notifying TopRetail and MediQ: "We've detected infra-level storage stalls causing tail latencies. We're moving your traffic to stable nodes and reverting a recent infra change. ETA 30-60m."

rollback-bot: revert-driver-194999 initiated by vikas. Targets: 9 hosts. Progress: 3/9 completed.

ke: also toggling NVMe scheduler from bfq -> mq-deadline and enabling IRQ coalescing tweaks on the noisy hosts as an emergency measure; observed initial avg wait drop ~20%.

toni: vendor engagement: opening case NVME-6102 with cloud provider and NVMe vendor. Attaching kernel traces, SMART output and controller logs. Asking whether controller firmware has known timeouts under mixed small-R/W + high submission queue depth.

vikas: after evicting traffic and rollback in progress, p95 for /v1/complete dropped from ~1.7s -> 260ms and p99 from ~9.8s -> 420ms on affected routes. Two hosts still draining due to long-lived sessions.

eli: billing-bot flagged: some customers ran retries which inflated token usage; please hold credits until we confirm session logs.

ke: root cause hypothesis: combination of driver 538.* changes + a controller firmware corner under heavy small-block load causing admin/completion queue stalls, which then triggered PCIe link resets and GPU DMA faults. The fault domain is storage-related but cascades to GPU availability.

toni: longer-term mitigations we propose: - add a 60m real-traffic canary for infra images that includes background blockstore operations, - implement per-host IO QoS (blkio or provider QoS), - tag nodes by NVMe firmware and avoid mixing firmware/driver combos during mass rollouts, - add per-disk completion-queue and admin-queue metric export. I'll own the QoS and metrics work.

vikas: rollout process change: split kernel and driver updates across separate canary slices plus require a 24h real-traffic window for infra-sensitive updates. Also require suspending scheduled snapshots during critical rollout windows.

toni: follow-ups: collect firmware revision matrix and add firmware-check to our instance onboarding; vendor recommended a non-disruptive firmware candidate but warned of scheduling constraints.

eli: customer comms: TopRetail and MediQ confirm improved latencies after traffic moved; requested RCA and compensation. Drafting formal incident notice and credit plan.

rollback-bot: revert-driver-194999 completed on 9/9 hosts. Post-rollback checks: no new nvme controller resets in last 30m; p99 back to baseline.

eli: runbook items: create a "storage-induced GPU DMA failure" checklist: drain, rollback, suspend snapshots, toggle scheduler, vendor escalation, customer comms, and billing credit flow. I'll own runbook and postmortem doc.

ke: note for infra: add a 'preflight' fio-style test that runs during canary for 30m emulating small-block mixed IO concurrently with synthetic inference.

toni: vendor follow-up: vendor confirmed two controllers had media-handling firmware edge cases; recommended firmware update and staggered scheduling. We'll coordinate a maintenance window.

eli: closing: customer impact mitigated, rollbacks done, owner list assigned (toni: metrics & QoS, vikas: rollout policy, ke: vendor coord, eli: postmortem & billing). Postmortem to be published in #postmortems tomorrow. Thanks team :thumbsup:

ops-bot: thread auto-archived after inactivity.
